status: PLACEHOLDER — UNCALIBRATED — NO MEASURED DATA IN THIS FILE
warning: Every value below is the default, not a measurement. Nothing here has been observed on hardware. Do not cite this file as calibration data and do not let a green CI run imply it is populated. It is populated by the Phase 0 hardware rig, one row per device model, or it is not populated.
description: Maps a device model to its tx_power_cal class: the RSSI a reference receiver measures at 1 metre from that transmitter, quantised to the seven legal values.
default_rationale: Equals TX_REF_DBM in BANDING.md §1, so an uncalibrated device normalises to a zero offset. It is a neutral guess, not a correct one.
quantisation_rule: Clamp the measured 1 m RSSI to the nearest legal value before encoding. Never transmit an unquantised value — fine-grained calibration is a device-model fingerprint that survives every ephemeral ID rotation (SPEC.md §3.2).

measurement_procedure.note: Must be identical for every model or the table is worthless.
steps: Reference receiver at exactly 1.00 m, line of sight, both devices at 1.0 m height.
Free space: no bodies, walls, or metal within 2 m of the path.
Device under test advertising at its normal Radius foreground settings.
Collect at least 100 RSSI samples over at least 60 s.
Take the median, not the mean — RSSI distributions are skewed by multipath.
Repeat with the device rotated 90, 180 and 270 degrees; take the median of medians. Antenna orientation matters more than most people expect.
Quantise to the nearest legal value and record the raw median alongside it.
measurement_procedure.simulator_note: A simulator has no radio and no antenna. There is no meaningful sense in which it can produce a calibration value.

resolution_order: 1. Exact match on platform + model identifier.

Implementations MUST NOT infer a calibration value from anything observed over the radio. Inferring the peer's model from its radio behaviour would rebuild exactly the fingerprint that quantisation exists to suppress (BANDING.md §3).
open_question: How large is the real spread across our target device set? Published figures for comparable programmes suggest roughly 30 dB (-45 to -75). If our measured spread is materially wider, the seven-value grid is too coarse and the accuracy-versus-fingerprint trade in SPEC.md §3.2 needs revisiting with real numbers.
